fossil
The papersThe code

DNA-binding proteins by PSSM distance, dug back up.

Xu and colleagues told DNA-binding proteins from others by their evolutionary profiles. The code and the web server are gone. We rebuilt the method from the paper, made the 1,261 profiles again against a 2014 protein database, and checked 28 of its 34 results.

Our curve has the published level (ACC 0.76 to 0.79, MCC 0.53 to 0.59) and is as flat, but single values move by up to 0.02 between 5-fold splits, more than most gaps to the paper.

Our largest pair weights are (G,G), (G,D), (G,P) and (N,P); (R,R), (R,P), (P,R) and (A,R) rank 326, 333, 133 and 176 of 400. Products of raw log-odds scores do not grow with arginine content (two negative R scores multiply to a large positive), and no variant of Eq. 12 we tried brings the four pairs to the top. Read as a linear grey scale, the published Fig. 2A itself ranks (A,R) about eighth. The five occurrences come back; the text gives three of their lags off by one ((R,R) lg 3 for lg 2, (P,R) lg 2 and 3 for lg 3 and 4). Whether all five lie in the DNA-binding region depends on how the region is drawn, which the paper does not say: by contact with the DNA in the crystal structure, (R,R) lg 1 (R25, R26) is 13.2 A away, so four are in and one is out; by the span of contacts, all five are in.

Our PSSM-DT curve stays within 2.2 points of true positive rate of the published one (AUC 86.34 against 86.50): equal at 5 and 40% false positives, 1 to 2 points lower between 15 and 30%, where our specificity is lower. At 2 px that is enough to clear the wrong-input control by only a little. Same causes as Table 1. Our comparator curves lie above the published ones, as the AUCs of Table 2 do (for example AvePscore-20 85.68 against 81.40). The paper's implementations are not given beyond citations, so its lead of 6 ACC points shrinks to 0.56 in our run.

On PDB186 our model gets ACC 66.13 and AUC 74.44 against the paper's 80.00 and 87.40, below DBPPred (76.88, 79.29). No identity threshold for the homology filter brings it back: AUC stays between 74.4 and 76.0 for thresholds of 25 to 99%, and only training on the unfiltered benchmark, which shares 42 chains with PDB186, reaches 81.49 (87.47 with UniRef90 PSSMs). The paper does not report how many chains its filter removed.

PSSM-DT comes back within about 2 points: ACC 78.88 against 79.96, SN 82.10 against 81.91 (one chain more), SP 75.82 against 78.00 (12 chains fewer), AUC 86.34 against 86.50. No value matches at the printed precision. Five printed ACC and MCC values do not follow from the printed SN and SP and are left out of the count. The PSSMs of the 2014 nr cannot be rebuilt; each other unstated setting moves ACC by at most 1.3 points and none closes the gap in all four metrics.

PSSM-DT still beats the four earlier encodings in our run, but by half a point, not six. The PDB186 result does not come back. Causes: the comparators the authors built in house, and a homology filter that cannot run as written.

What came back

The benchmark
All 1,075 chains, 525 and 550, read from the supplement.
PSSM-DT on the benchmark
ACC 78.88, SN 82.10, SP 75.82, AUC 86.34 by jackknife, within about 2 points of the paper.
Table 4, earlier predictors
Every row recomputed from the outputs Lou and colleagues published.
Fig. 5, three curves
DBPPred, DNABIND and DNAbinder drawn from those outputs land on the published curves.
The method
PSSM-DT as a Python package, the same as the authors' later toolkit computes it.

What stayed buried

  • The 2014 protein database the profiles were made from; nobody kept it.
  • DNA-Prot and iDNA-Prot as the authors rebuilt them.
  • The size of the paper's six point lead over the other encodings.
  • The PDB186 result: our model scores below the earlier predictors there.
  • The four amino-acid pairs of Fig. 2; our model weighs others.

PSSM-DT still beats the four earlier encodings in our run, but by half a point, not six. The PDB186 result does not come back. Causes: the comparators the authors built in house, and a homology filter that cannot run as written.

What we matched

Some numbers in the paper do not follow from its own tables. We list them so nobody chases them.

Table 1
Five of its ACC and MCC values do not follow from the printed SN and SP.
Table 4
SP 72.83 is not a share of 93 chains, and the MCC is printed as 0.647 and as 0.674.
Text
The gains over DBPPred, 3.105 and 0.136, do not follow from Table 4.
Fig. 2C
The text gives three of the five pairs the wrong distance, off by one.

Dug up in November 2026. The profiles took a night on a cluster; everything after them reruns in minutes.
